\subsection{Prior and posterior predictive checks}
\label{supp:ppc}

We assessed model adequacy with prior- and posterior-predictive checks for the
selected model (All-$h$ + voracious mixture). Figure~\ref{supp:prior} shows that
the calibrated priors cover the observed distribution of prey consumed at every
starting density $N_0$, without piling probability mass at the boundaries.
Figure~\ref{supp:post} overlays the posterior-predictive distribution of prey
eaten on the data for each $N_0$: the mixture reproduces both the central
tendency and the spike of fish that consume all available prey.

Table~\ref{supp:tab_bayes} reports posterior-predictive $p$-values for a set of
discrepancy statistics. The mixture is well calibrated for the full-consumption
fraction (overall and within light/moderate/heavy weight strata), the
zero-consumption fraction, and the mean number eaten. The one statistic it does
not fully capture is the total dispersion of counts across densities
($p_B \approx 0$): the model is slightly over-dispersed at low $N_0$ and
under-dispersed at high $N_0$, which is also visible as a mild $\cup$-shape in the
LOO probability-integral-transform (Fig.~\ref{supp:loopit}). We judged this
residual misfit minor relative to the risk of over-fitting a more elaborate
dispersion model, and it does not affect the treatment-effect estimates.

Figures~\ref{supp:violin}--\ref{supp:warmedweek} show discrepancy checks
disaggregated by fish weight, acclimation condition, experimental condition, and
the warmed$\times$6-week cell of particular biological interest; observed values
fall within the posterior-predictive envelopes in each case.
